name: Kaleva

sources.title: Kaleva (airplane) — Junkers Ju 52/3m OH-ALL of Aero O/Y, shot down over the Gulf of Finland on 14 June 1940; the remains found north of Keri in June 2024
Al Jazeera (2024) — Divers find remains of Finnish WWII plane shot down by Soviets: the landing gear, one of the engines and parts of the wings, at about 70 m
Postimees (2024) — Divers believe they have found the wreck: in pieces on a rocky bottom of ridges and hollows, north of Keri
Aviation Safety Network — Junkers Ju-52/3mge OH-ALL, 14 June 1940
Junkers Ju 52 — the type: three radial engines, corrugated duralumin skin, the Junkers double wing; 18.9 m long, 29.25 m span

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1464299_kaleva.py; tools/airkit.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. The remains, in pieces among outcrops of rock: the left wing outboard of the engine, torn off and upside down; a piece of the right wing with its flap; the left wing engine with its propeller blades bent back; a landing gear leg with its wheel; the tailplane and part of the fin; strips of the corrugated fuselage skin all about; the two other engines deep in the bottom. Dressed with tools/dresskit.py: its own sediment (painted by Offlined with the seabed colour), the dulled aluminium with a film of silt, the scant life of the deep Baltic, textures and baked light. model_built.glb: the airliner as she flew in 1940, natural metal, OH-ALL on the fuselage and the wings, KALEVA by the cockpit, standing on her wheels. Approximate: only the gear, one engine and parts of the wings have been described, so the other pieces and the places of all of them are a reconstruction; the airframe follows the general drawings of the Ju 52/3m.
